# `silk/http/serve`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A fast HTTP/1.1 server: write one handler function, and serve it on every core.

## When to use
Use this module to answer HTTP requests with little code and high throughput. Write a handler
that reads a [`Request`](#Request) and writes a [`Response`](#Response), then call [`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve), or
[`Server.serveTls`](#Server.impl.serveTls) for HTTPS. For streaming bodies, upgrades or full control of the
connection, use `silk.http.server` instead.

## Details
[`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve) runs the `silk.net.tcp_server` engine: one event loop for each worker thread,
and no locks between workers. The server reads a whole request, with its body, before it calls
the handler. Requests that come one after another on the same connection (pipelining) are
answered in order.

The server parses HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1 requests with a `Content-Length` body, a `chunked` body,
or no body. It answers with HTTP/1.1 and adds the `Date`, `Content-Length` and, when it closes
the connection, `Connection: close` header fields. A request with `Expect: 100-continue` gets
`100 Continue` before its body is read. A `HEAD` request gets the head of the response, without
the body.

The connection closes after the response when the request asks for it, or when the request is
HTTP/1.0 without `Connection: keep-alive`. A request that the server cannot read gets an error
response, and then the connection closes:

| Status | Cause |
|---|---|
| 400 | The request line, a header field or the body framing is malformed |
| 413 | The body is larger than `maxBodyBytes` |
| 431 | The head is larger than `maxHeadBytes`, or has more than `maxHeaderFields` fields |
| 501 | The transfer coding is not `chunked` |
| 505 | The version is not HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1 |

## Errors
[`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve) fails with `TcpServerError` if a listener cannot be made, and with
`OutOfMemoryError` if a worker cannot allocate. A failure of a handler only ends its request: the
server answers `500 Internal Server Error` and closes that connection.

## Gotchas
- It needs Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64, like `silk.net.tcp_server`.
- The handler runs on the worker thread of the connection. A handler that blocks, for example on
  a slow file, stops every other connection of that worker until it returns.
- [`Request`](#Request) and its texts borrow the input buffer. They are valid only during the handler.

## Examples
### Answer every request
```silk,no_run
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.http.serve { Handler, Request, Response, Server }

struct Hello {}

impl Handler for Hello {
  effect fn handle(self: &Self, request: &Request<'_>, response: &mut Response<'_>) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
    if request.path() == "/" {
      run response.text("Hello, World!")
      return ()
    }
    response.status(404)
    run response.text("Not found")
  }
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 { drop error return 1 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let served = Server.make(8080).serve(Hello {})
  return run Effect.catchAll(Effect.map(move served, fn(done: ()) -> i32 { return 0 }), failed)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `Server` with `import silk.http.serve { Server }`.

## `Request`

```silk
pub struct Request<'a>
```

One HTTP request, with its whole body.

### Details
The texts it returns borrow the input buffer of the connection, so they cost no copy. The
method, the target and the header names are ASCII, as the parser checks. Header values may hold
bytes that are not UTF-8: [`Request.header`](#Request.impl.header) skips such a value, and
[`Request.headerBytes`](#Request.impl.headerBytes) returns it.

<a id="Response"></a>

## `Response`

```silk
pub struct Response<'a>
```

The response to one [`Request`](#Request).

### Details
Set the status with [`Response.status`](#Response.impl.status) and add header fields with [`Response.header`](#Response.impl.header). Then
write the body with [`Response.send`](#Response.impl.send), [`Response.text`](#Response.impl.text) or [`Response.html`](#Response.impl.html). The server adds
`Date` and `Content-Length`. A handler that returns without a body sends an empty one, with the
status it set.

### Gotchas
- The body can be sent once. Later sends and header fields are ignored.
- [`Response.header`](#Response.impl.header) skips a field whose name is not a token or whose value has a line break,
  and the `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection` and `Date` fields, which the
  server writes itself.

Adds the header field `name: value`.

#### Details
It skips the field if the name is not a token, if the value holds a CR, an LF or a NUL, or if
the name is one the server writes itself: `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`
or `Date`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the field cannot be stored.

<a id="Handler"></a>

## `Handler`

```silk
pub interface Handler
```

The code that answers requests. [`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve) calls `handle` for each request.

### Details
One handler value serves every worker thread through a shared borrow, so the type must be
`Transferable` and `Concurrent`. Keep state that requests change in a `Mutex` or in atomics.

<a id="Handler.handle"></a>

### Operation `handle`

```silk
effect fn handle(self: &Self, request: &Request<'_>, response: &mut Response<'_>) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads `request` and writes `response`. A failure makes the server answer 500 and close the
connection.

<a id="Server"></a>

## `Server`

```silk
pub struct Server
```

An HTTP server, with the settings of [`ServerOptions`](#ServerOptions).

### Details
[`Server.make`](#Server.impl.make) gives the defaults for a port. The other functions return a copy with one
setting changed, so calls chain: `Server.make(8080).host("0.0.0.0").workers(4)`.

<a id="Server.impl.serve"></a>

### Method `serve`

```silk
pub effect<'static> fn serve<H: 'static + Handler + Transferable + Concurrent>(self: Self, handler: H) -> () ! ServeError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Serves `handler` on every worker, until a worker fails.

#### Details
The handler gets each request and writes its response. One handler value serves every
worker through a shared borrow, so it must be `Transferable` and `Concurrent`: a function, or
a closure that captures only such values, such as an `Arc` of a `Mutex`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidHost` if [`Server.host`](#Server.impl.host) got a text that is not an address.
- `Engine` if a listener, a thread or an event loop cannot be made, for example when the port
  is in use.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a worker cannot allocate.

<a id="Server.impl.serveTls"></a>

### Method `serveTls`

```silk
pub effect<'static> fn serveTls<H: 'static + Handler + Transferable + Concurrent>(
    self: Self,
    config: TlsServerConfig,
    handler: H,
  ) -> () ! ServeError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Serves `handler` over HTTPS with the certificate and key of `config`, until a worker fails.

#### Details
Each connection runs TLS 1.3 with `silk.tls.server` (through `silk.tls.server_protocol`), then HTTP/1.1 over it, as
[`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve) does. Load `config` with `TlsServerConfig.fromPem`.

#### Errors
The same as [`Server.serve`](#Server.impl.serve).
